objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares C functions operating on wchar_t strings. As a placeholder, note that there are no custom data types to document.

functions.name: wcslen_fixed
functions.description: Returns the length, in wide characters, of the null-terminated wide string s, excluding the terminating L'\0'. Intended as a fixed/portable variant of wcslen; comments in the header suggest these wide-string utilities may treat data as UTF-32 even when wchar_t is 16-bit, but exact encoding semantics are not documented.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated wide string (wchar_t*).
The pointed-to memory must be readable up to and including the first terminating L'\0'.
Behavior for non-terminated buffers is undefined and may overread.
Return value is the number of wide characters before the terminator; no error reporting is specified.

functions.name: wcsncmp_fixed
functions.signature: int wcsncmp_fixed(const wchar_t *s1, const wchar_t * s2, size_t n);
functions.description: Lexicographically compares up to n wide characters of the null-terminated wide strings s1 and s2. Semantics mirror standard wcsncmp (negative/zero/positive result), with this "fixed" variant intended for consistent behavior across platforms; the header notes these utilities may expect UTF-32 code units even when wchar_t is 16-bit, but exact normalization or case rules are not documented.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be non-null pointers to readable wide strings (wchar_t*).
Each input must be readable up to at least n wide characters or until a terminating L'\0' is encountered, whichever comes first.
n is the maximum number of wide characters to compare; it may be zero.
The strings should be null-terminated if their length is less than n; otherwise reading up to n wide characters must be valid.
Return value follows standard comparison semantics (<0, 0, >0); no separate error indicator is provided.

functions.name: wcsstr_fixed
functions.signature: wchar_t* wcsstr_fixed(const wchar_t* haystack, const wchar_t* needle);
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of the wide-string needle in the wide-string haystack and returns a pointer to the beginning of the match within haystack, or NULL if not found. Intended as a fixed/portable variant of wcsstr; the header comments suggest these utilities may operate on UTF-32 code units even where wchar_t is 16-bit, but exact encoding handling is not specified.
requirements: haystack must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated wide string (wchar_t*).
needle must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated wide string (wchar_t*).
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points into haystack; the lifetime of haystack must outlive use of the returned pointer.
If needle is an empty string (L""), behavior is expected to mirror standard wcsstr (returns haystack), but exact behavior is not explicitly documented.
No error parameter or exception is specified; NULL indicates no match.

data_types.description: A buffer of arbitrary bytes with no required encoding or structure. May contain any values including null bytes. In these stubs, the raw bytes are consumed and mapped deterministically into wide characters; the data is not required to be valid text or follow any specific format.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We need to generate an arbitrary byte string that the fuzz harness maps into wchar_t sequences.
# The stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; each call receives an independent buffer, but
# the fuzzer framework will seed them from the same initial bytes we return. To make this initial
# buffer useful across all stubs:
# - Include several sections with varied byte patterns (ASCII, high bytes, zeros, repeats, ramps,
#   Unicode-like sequences, surrogate-looking pairs, mixed endian pairs), so that when the harness
#   constructs wchar_t values by XORing and shifting pairs of bytes, it gets diverse non-zero values
#   and also controllable zeros at times.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given seed, but with randomness to explore variety across runs.

ASCII_BLOCK = (
    b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    b"0123456789"
    b" _-:/.,;!@#$%^&*()+={}[]<>?|'\"\\\n\r\t"
)

# Some multi-byte UTF-8 sequences, including BMP and non-BMP when interpreted as UTF-8.
UTF8_BLOCK = (
    "\u00A9 \u00AE \u03B1\u03B2\u03B3 \u0410\u0411\u0412 "
    "\u20AC \u2603 \u2764 \u0E01\u0E02\u0E03 "
    "\U0001F600\U0001F642\U0001F680"
).encode("utf-8")

# Create surrogate-like pairs and high bytes to influence wide char construction.
def make_high_byte_block() -> bytes:
    # Alternating high/low bytes and zero bytes to create patterns that, when combined as
    # ((b1 << 8) ^ b0), yield varied ranges and also some zeros when b1<<8 == b0.
    out = bytearray()
    for hb in (0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xA5, 0xC3, 0xE1, 0xFF):
        for lb in (0x00, 0x01, 0x10, 0x55, 0xAA, 0xFE, 0xFF):
            out.append(hb)
            out.append(lb)
    return bytes(out)

# Repeating single-byte runs encourage long equal wchar_t sequences after mapping.
def make_runs(byte_val: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([byte_val]) * length

# Ramps help produce strictly increasing/decreasing sequences.
def make_ramp(start: int, step: int, count: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start + i * step) & 0xFF for i in range(count)))

# Insert occasional zeros to allow the harness to sometimes create L'\0' before it intentionally avoids it.
def sparse_zeros(count: int, gap: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(count):
        out.extend(make_ramp(i, 13, gap - 1))
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

# Build segments likely to trigger interesting behavior in wcsstr and wcsncmp by embedding repeated motifs
# and overlaps so that needles may or may not appear in haystacks depending on seed.
def motif_block(motif: bytes, repeats: int, pad: bytes) -> bytes:
    return (motif + pad) * repeats + motif

def shuffle_chunks(rnd: random.Random, chunks: List[bytes]) -> List[bytes]:
    idx = list(range(len(chunks)))
    rnd.shuffle(idx)
    return [chunks[i] for i in idx]

# Ensure final length capped <= 4096
MAX_LEN = 4096
MIN_LEN = 128


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Core building blocks
    chunks.append(ASCII_BLOCK)
    chunks.append(UTF8_BLOCK)
    chunks.append(make_high_byte_block())

    # Repeats and ramps
    chunks.append(make_runs(0x00, rnd.randint(8, 64)))  # explicit zero runs
    chunks.append(make_runs(0xFF, rnd.randint(16, 96)))
    chunks.append(make_runs(0x7F, rnd.randint(16, 96)))
    chunks.append(make_ramp(rnd.randint(0, 255), rnd.choice([1, 3, 5, 7, 11]), 128))
    chunks.append(make_ramp(rnd.randint(0, 255), -rnd.choice([1, 2, 4, 8]), 128))

    # Sparse zeros to occasionally create terminators in derived wchar_t mapping (harness tries to avoid early zeros)
    chunks.append(sparse_zeros(12, rnd.randint(4, 12)))

    # Motifs beneficial for substring search and comparisons
    motifA = b"ABCD" * 4
    motifB = b"\x00\xAA\x00\xAA"  # alternating with zeros
    motifC = b"xyzXYZ" * 3
    padA = b"-" * rnd.randint(3, 9)
    padB = bytes([0xFF]) * rnd.randint(2, 6)
    padC = make_ramp(0x10, 0x10, rnd.randint(4, 12))
    chunks.append(motif_block(motifA, rnd.randint(2, 6), padA))
    chunks.append(motif_block(motifB, rnd.randint(2, 6), padB))
    chunks.append(motif_block(motifC, rnd.randint(2, 6), padC))

    # Include some 2-byte pairs that, when combined as ((b1<<8)^b0), yield common letters/numbers
    # Solve for b0 given desired v and chosen b1.
    def mk_pairs_for_values(values: List[int], b1: int) -> bytes:
        out = bytearray()
        for v in values:
            b0 = (v ^ (b1 << 8)) & 0xFF
            out.append(b0)
            out.append(b1 & 0xFF)
        return bytes(out)

    target_vals = [ord('A'), ord('B'), ord('C'), ord('a'), ord('z'), ord('0'), ord('9'), 0x0100, 0x03B1]
    chunks.append(mk_pairs_for_values(target_vals, 0x12))
    chunks.append(mk_pairs_for_values(target_vals, 0x34))

    # Add some random noise blocks to diversify across seeds, but keep deterministic
    for _ in range(5):
        size = rnd.randint(64, 256)
        block = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
        chunks.append(block)

    # Shuffle chunks to vary layout per seed
    chunks = shuffle_chunks(rnd, chunks)

    # Concatenate and trim/pad to a reasonable total length
    data = b"".join(chunks)

    # Target length biased between 512 and 3072, capped at 4096
    target_len = rnd.randint(512, 3072)
    if target_len > MAX_LEN:
        target_len = MAX_LEN

    # If too long, truncate; if too short, extend with additional patterned data
    if len(data) > MAX_LEN:
        data = data[:MAX_LEN]
    elif len(data) < max(MIN_LEN, target_len):
        # Extend with alternating noise and ramps to reach target
        need = max(MIN_LEN, target_len) - len(data)
        # Compose in chunks until satisfied
        tail = bytearray()
        while len(tail) < need:
            choice = rnd.randrange(4)
            if choice == 0:
                tail.extend(bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(min(256, need - len(tail)))))
            elif choice == 1:
                tail.extend(make_ramp(rnd.randint(0, 255), rnd.choice([1, 5, 9, 13]), min(256, need - len(tail))))
            elif choice == 2:
                tail.extend(make_runs(rnd.randint(0, 255), min(128, need - len(tail))))
            else:
                tail.extend(sparse_zeros(rnd.randint(2, 6), rnd.randint(3, 10)))
        data += bytes(tail[:need])

    # Final hard cap
    data = data[:MAX_LEN]

    return data
